sources.title: Bethesda Is Already Selling The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Merch
sources.text: Hot on the heels of Bethesda Game Studios officially announcing the full name of its highly anticipated next project, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the developer has already put up merch for the upcoming RPG on its online shop. You can be the first person in your friend group with a Sentinel-logo hoodie or T-shirt. And like the Ford Model T, it comes in any color you want, as long as it's black. The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel hoodie is $64.99, while the identical item in T-shirt form is $34.99. Hat tip to @MrMattyPlays on X for first spotting the Sentinel merch. Bethesda says, "Celebrate The Elder Scrolls VI. Your next journey through Tamriel will be in The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Show off your excitement with the official hoodie!" And if you're interesteed in ordering, note the disclaimer: "This hoodie runs small. For the perfect fit, we recommend ordering one size larger than your usual size." The T-shirt shares an identical description, minus the note about it running small. You'll have plenty of time to break in either of these clothing items, as Sentinel isn't expected to be released for at least a couple more years . That would mean it might be at least a decade between the original announcement of The Elder Scrolls 6 and the time it's finally on your hard drive. Regardless, it's arguably the biggest game Xbox has in its portfolio by a country mile and when the release date finally arrives, it's going to be a very, very big deal. Amidst all of the changes at Xbox this year, it will be interesting to see if, a) The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel will be available on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on day one, b) if it might line up with the launch of Xbox's next-gen Project Helix console/gaming PC hybrid , and/or c) if it ends up being an Xbox console exclusive . Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Eight years ago the idea of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel had me captivated, but can Bethesda recapture the magic?
sources.text: Eight years ago, I sat at my desk enthralled. Bethesda had just released the first trailer for The Elder Scrolls 6 , a then mysteriously nameless, locationless sequel to one of the biggest games of all time, and I reckoned I'd just found the secrets to both. It was going to be set in the region of Hammerfell, I reckoned . And the city of Sentinel was a crucial factor in reasoning why. Admittedly, I'm maybe a little more horrified at my level of Elder Scrolls obsession than I am chuffed at any apparent clairvoyance. Ultimately it was a bit of a punt, launched off the back of a day's worth of fanatical hyperfocus and exactly the right amount of the old Gamer Network office's weapons-grade filter coffee. "There's not really a lot to go on here", I wrote, sagely, "but, if we had to, we'd plant our flag in Hammerfell as the location of The Elder Scrolls 6 ." Indulge me a bit and let's retread the reasoning. First, three assumptions were required in order to make any kind of guess at all: The Elder Scrolls 6 would not be set in all of Tamriel; not set outside of Tamriel; and would be set somewhere vaguely close in the timeline to the events of Morrowind , Oblivion and Skyrim - so as to make that bit of scrabbly rock and ruined castle, visible in that now infamous first teaser, at least somewhat traceable with contemporary descriptions in the lore. Then came a lot of narrowing down. Not Morrowind, Cyrodiil, Skyrim or the Summerset Isles, I decided, as we'd been to all of those too recently (I'll leave it up to you whether another eight years since Morrowind lets that one still count as remotely "recent", but still). And then not Valenwood, Elsweyr, or Black Marsh, thanks to the topography of the land in the trailer and the type of environment on show. That left High Rock and Hammerfell, the former of which we ruled out because of its relative size - on the small side for a presumably beefy new TES game - and more importantly, the architecture that seemed at odds with the sandy stone just barely visible in the structures of that first teaser. And finally: Sentinel. The city was perfectly positioned - along a coast with the sea to the right, dry mountains in the foreground, warm stone ruins to the left, no visible land beyond. Now, that setting is all but confirmed - "all but" as, technically , nothing's set in stone yet, pardon the pun. All we've since been shown is a sand dune, an Elder Scroll, the name Sentinel, and a brief quote from a Moth Priest to a Hammerfell High Queen. But we can pretty much lock it in. To the Elder Scrolls obsessive who spent that day eight years ago scurrying down endless YouTube rabbit holes and lingering on the dustiest unofficial wiki pages, the thought of a game set there ought to be tantalising. Already, even with that paper thin new teaser, there's enough to start picking at. The new trailer's quote is dated just four years after the events of Skyrim, for instance, with both that territory and Cyrodiil located right next door, making for some lovely opportunities for crossovers and references to wider events. And the quote itself is curious. As our guides team have already speculated , the notion of "A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate" gives off the faintest whiff of a time-forking Dragon Break. That being the timeline-branching, multiple-player-choice-enabling thing that happened at the end of The Elder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall, a game which took place - aha! - in the Iliac Bay between High Rock and Hammerfell. Surely, the same bay we're looking at in that original TES 6 trailer. It keeps going! The "victory" mentioned in that quote could refer to the victory won by the people of Hammerfell against a Thalmor invasion, in a conflict that - ooh! - took place around the same time Skyrim's main story was happening, and just a few years before that quote is dated. Could we get branching timelines? A tying together of the overarching Thalmor plotline that's been simmering away until now? A load of varying endings, as Bethesda experimented with so openly in Starfield ? I'm off again. Fire up the Unofficial Elder Scrolls Pages! There's such magic here, far beyond the apparent mastery Bethesda has over theory-baiting teasers for suckers like me. These games, for instance, also have an uncanny knack for joyful stupidity. There are Oblivion NPC barks out there that landed right as YouTube's golden era hit liftoff, and in turn defined an entire generation's sense of humour. I was once in a Slack channel here called # reeblereeblereeble , which was just myself and two other writers punting Imperial Watch taunts at each other to lighten the mood every couple of weeks, or whenever someone seemed a bit stressed. When I leave a gathering of old school friends I still catch myself bidding them "farewell!" with Wood Elf gusto, and giggling at the thought of being immediately squished into mulch . And none of that is to mention the design itself, which has at times been more or less unparalleled. The clockwork, systemic magic of Morrowind is extraordinary, the first hour alone a lesson - at least as important as good old over-cited Mario 1:1 - in instructional design. Within a walkable radius of the musty little settlement of Seyda Neen Bethesda gave the player every tool necessary for understanding - and subsequently playing with, then outright breaking - its entire world. With Oblivion it brought the role-playing open world to the masses. With Skyrim it expanded what our very concept of the masses means. By all accounts I should, then, be absolutely drooling at the thought of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel. But for some reason the excitement is muted. It's been like this since long before this second teaser, frankly, and for much of that time I've put it down to Bethesda itself. Bethesda Game Studios has not been on a good run. Fallout 76 might've finally recovered from its nightmarish launch, but time hasn't been hugely kind to Fallout 4 , which longer

sources.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel fans ponder split timelines, alternative histories, and more as story speculation runs wild following latest teaser
sources.text: Following the release of yesterday's brief new The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel teaser trailer , story speculation is running rampant across communities dedicated to the fantasy series, with fans theorising everything from alternative histories to split timelines. Yesterday's teaser - which arrived as part of Bethesda's 40th anniversary celebrations and comes amid devastating cuts across Xbox's first-party studios - was minimal. It opened with a shot of desert sand, before revealing the subtitle 'Sentinel' and ending with a quote from an unknown character. It's not much to go on, but is proving just enough to encourage discussion around what may be in store for Bethesda's next RPG. And a good place to start is that quote. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes," it reads. "A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate." All this is attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, , but some fans think the accompanying date - 4E 206 - might be just as significant. "[Sentinel] likely takes place five or more years after the start of Skyrim," hypothesised Reddit user 04nc1n9 . "Hammerfell is a monarchy, it hasn't changed to any other political system after their imperial secession. The monarchy of Hammerfell has a Moth Priest on hand, even though the Moth Priests are generally an Imperial thing. Hammerfell's monarch has access to an Elder Scroll after the Elder Scrolls scattered." This unexpected link between Moth Priests and Hammerfell's High Queen has created speculation of its own. One theory, combined with the proximity of Sentinel's story to that of Skyrim, has the Thalmor play a key role. "[It's] likely the Thalmor being the antagonists with so little time having passed," wrote user Jonesketi, " and with justifiable knowledge of how to cause great harm with the Elder Scrolls, [this] would've prompted [Hammerfell] to begin their own preparations. [The Thalmor are] also such a fitting antagonist since we didn't get to kick them down in Skyrim, which would offer catharsis if it came in Sentinel." As for the quote itself, its vague wording has inspired some particularly out-there speculation. Some fans are looking back to previously vanquished forces in the series, in light of the phrase "a victory undone", and are theorising it might refer to a Dragon Break - an in-universe timeline split in which multiple events can all occur and simultaneously be true once the timelines reconverge. In previous games, Dragon Breaks have served as a handy explanation for the multiple endings. Talk of "undone" events set user Wafelze's mind to the Numidium, a giant mechanical golem whose activation in The Elder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall caused its own Dragon Break. "With how important time is to Skyrim’s story," they speculated, "it wouldn’t surprise me if this story is about time being entirely broken." "See, I'm thinking it has to do with the creation of Nirn and Lorkhan," wrote Potential Film 7140 . "The Altmer hate Lorkhan and men see the creation of the world as a victory. The elves did not ... maybe they'll try to undo what created the divines so they can go back to their original ancestry. Wildly out-there take but that's what my brain tells me." What's more, the theories around split timelines and the Thalmor have converged with thoughts of a possible 'Man in the High Castle'-style alternate history setting for Sentinel, unfolding in a version of the world where the Thalmor have power. "Maybe the Empire originally held together after Oblivion, and the Thalmor used some cheater Elder Scroll magic to rewrite history so that they dunked on the Empire," suggested Original League 6094 . "Or if I recall, Hammerfell was doing a great job beating the Thalmor as of Skyrim. Maybe the version of events got overwritten and now Hammerfell is under Thalmor subjugation, and the Elder Scroll is giving her glimpses of the timeline where Hammerfell won." Will these theories prove to be true? With the launch of Sentinel still reportedly years away, it could be some time before we find out. But if nothing else, this feverish story speculation suggests there's a major hunger among fans for information - any information - about Sentinel. And that's no real surprise. After all, yesterday's teaser was only the second official look at a game whose reveal has been dragging on for over eight years now.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel won't fill the shoes of GTA 6 as the next white whale, says analyst
sources.text: This November has been a terrific month for the number six, with GTA 6 approaching and The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel finally out in the open. Once GTA 6 is in our hands at last, we'll have to reckon with a strange new world where we're no longer constantly waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto – the kind of alien sensation that Hollow Knight: Silksong players, who practically grieved yearning after so much buildup, are intimately familiar with. Will The Elder Scrolls 6 step up to the plate as the next [clears throat] Massive Sequel Over a Decade in the Making That Also Has the Number Six in It ? Is it going to fill Rockstar's enormous shoes as gaming's white whale? "No, I don't think it is," says Circana games analyst Mat Piscatella when I mention this idea in passing. "It's a huge game, obviously, but things like Grand Theft Auto, Call of Duty, NBA 2K, these are games that are huge, mass-market appeal titles." This reflects part of what makes GTA 6 so interesting, not as a game to be played but as an outlier to be observed. Similar to Nintendo, Rockstar can basically do whatever it wants because its loyal audience is big enough. More uniquely, Grand Theft Auto is the type of game that appeals to a huge range of players, from the enthusiasts playing dozens of the best games of 2026 to casual fans who mostly stick to the sports and shooter series that Piscatella mentions. "They're their own thing," he says. "It's a different set of rules, a different set of expectations. They're gonna do their thing, and they've earned every bit of that, just based on what they've done. Nintendo is its own thing, too. They are unique, and I know people hate that and go, 'They're competing just like everyone else.' They are, but with the IP and their history and how they've developed how they go to market, it is a unique proposition. That's why they can do things other companies can't, and they have a relationship with their players that other platforms don't. These are companies or developers that are doing their own thing, blazing their own trail, and a lot of other people try to follow." As AAA game development faces cost crises, Rockstar is making the biggest bet of all, and with the most favorable odds imaginable. Nobody else could make a game like GTA 6. For anyone but Rockstar, it would be too big to succeed. "If you want to talk about a big bet, they don't come any bigger than this, and the appetite for big bets like this doesn't exist in many places," says Piscatella. Even The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, follow-up to one of the most-played RPGs of all time, and handily the most-modded, is in a different weight class. (The Witcher 3 and Skyrim have both sold 65 million copies .) Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more "Whether you're talking about an Elder Scrolls, a Witcher, a God of War, those are big games but they're nowhere near the scale of an NBA 2K, Call of Duty, or Grand Theft Auto," adds Piscatella. "No shade to them. They're all great games and perform very well. But we're talking about a secondary tier to those real mass-market hit drivers." It certainly doesn't help that The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced eight years ago, and re-announced this week with a subtitle, yet we still don't even have a screenshot. The game is reportedly looking at a 2029 launch , which would put it 18 years post-Skyrim, so I'm going to need Bethesda to wake me up for the third time when, and only when, it's got some heat. Bethesda wants you to "show off your excitement" for The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel by spending $35 on a T-shirt Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: Rockstar shares 38 new screenshots of Grand Theft Auto 6, showing off Vice City, Jason and Lucia, and much more
sources.text: Rockstar Games have released 38 new screenshots of Grand Theft Auto 6 , ahead of its release later this month. These screenshots, found on a dedicated launch gallery website Rockstar has created , prompts viewers to scroll down and take in the sights of several high quality in-game screenshots snapshotting all kinds of people, places, and events. These include, but are not limited to, a DJ set in-action, a man and his pitbull looking tough to the camera, a tattooed man getting his hair done (machine gun on hand), and a daring motorbike escape. However, my personal favourite has got to be a lively shot of a dive bar. A band - seemingly called The Rusty Anchor is playing - and some older ladies appear to be having a friendly chat with an open-shirt-wearing geezer enjoying a beer. You can find all the new images in an image gallery below. So look through them at your pleasure: Grand Theft Auto 6 is due to release on the 19th November on the PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. A few days prior, Rockstar employees are voting on whether or not they'd like to officially recognise a developer union , as the Rockstar vs IWBG union employment tribunal comes to a close on the eve of GTA 6's release date.

sources.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: The Most Requested Update – New Game+, Rune Forge Update, New Resource, and More
sources.text: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s The Most Requested Update is now live on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX One. This update brings several exciting new features to the game, giving you new ways to enjoy your Viking adventure. The Most Requested Update is centered around the addition of New Game+, one of the most fan-requested features for Assassin’s Creed Valhalla . The other features included in the patch all ensure that your endgame and New Game+ experience is fresh and challenging, with rewards that make it worth your while. Here’s what you can expect to find in The Most Requested Update: We spoke to Lead Game Designer David Larouche to learn more about the update and how the team keeps players at the forefront of everything they do. David Larouche : The New Game+ feature was definitely the most requested feature from fans. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a massive game, but for some, playing it once is not enough. With this update, we are incredible excited to now allow our most dedicated Vikings to play through the adventure once again, but this time, with their endgame character. DL : We wanted the New Game+ experience to not simply be a do-over; we wanted to allow players to keep climbing in power, feel a more granular progression, and to keep improving their characters. For all those reasons, we added an extended progression mode, further upgrades on all pieces of divine gear, a new tier of rune and over 300 possible new rune perks that can be engraved in the rune forge – and all of those features are available without New Game+ as well. With all those additional features, we believe that the New Game+ experience will encourage players to push Eivor to their full potential. DL : I think the most surprising thing to us was that there weren’t really any big challenges that had us stumped. We managed to put a really strong team of devs who are experienced in adding New Game+ onto already existing games; the production process was incredibly smooth. DL : With the update, we’ve added basically every single perk that was on an item as a rune that can be engraved in the rune forge, regardless of if it was released in the extended experience, from an expansion, or even from the Store. I can’t wait to see how players use all of these different perks together and create all sorts of different synergies. I’m sure there are many overpowered combinations to be found! DL : Valhalla may have released its final content update years ago, but that doesn’t mean players stopped caring about the game, and neither did we. We know New Game+ is something the community has wanted for a long time, and when the opportunity came up to finally make it happen, we couldn’t wait to pursue it . [MB1] [BS2] Ultimately, it’s about giving longtime players another reason to return to a world they’ve invested so much time in, and to experience Eivor’s journey again from a different perspective while bringing along much of what they’ve earned along the way. The fact that some time has passed doesn’t make that experience any less meaningful to us, or, hopefully, to our players. DL : Community is incredibly important to me and to the team. Personally, I check social networks regularly to see what players are talking about, and as a team, we pay close attention to feedback and conversations across the internet. We love seeing what players create and share around our games. That connection with community is incredibly rewarding, and it’s a big part of why we do what we do. Play Assassin’s Creed Valhalla : The Most Requested Update today on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX One.

sources.name: PlayStation Blog
sources.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: new update brings New Game Plus, upgraded PSSR support for PS5 Pro today
sources.text: Ubisoft outlines what upgraded PSSR brings to the PS5 Pro version of the game. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla : The Most Requested Update, a free update bringing several player-requested and quality-of-life features to the game, is live today on PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro. The update has new content, a progression update, and more, including: The new PSSR update is exclusive to PlayStation 5 Pro players, giving them an even higher visual quality as they embark on or continue their Viking adventures in England. We spoke to Priscilla Nguyen, Engineering Studio Manager, to learn more about this update and why it’s essential for PlayStation 5 Pro players. Priscilla Nguyen : It was about integrating the upgraded PSSR into the game, to have better graphics when upscaling at a better framerate. The upgraded PSSR is more efficient than the original, and easier to implement in the game source code. The upgraded PSSR is an enhanced version, and slightly more efficient than the game’s current Temporal Upscaler. More importantly, it’s much crisper and more visually stable, giving you seamless and stunning environments to explore in England. PN: At Ubisoft, it is important to remain at the forefront of technological innovation to ensure players continue to benefit from the best possible gaming experience, and as the upgraded PSSR was already successfully integrated into our latest releases, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and Assassin’s Creed Shadows, we thought it would be great to have in Valhalla too. The Assassin’s Creed Valhalla update presented an excellent opportunity to integrate the upgraded PSSR, delivering a noticeably sharper and more visually refined image quality in 4K and smoothness with 60FPS. One of the aspects players appreciated most about Assassin’s Creed Valhalla was the beauty and visual variety of its open world, from the snowy mountains of Norway to the flourishing meadows, robust forests, and frigid highlands of England. Now, with the new PSSR optimizations, those graphics have been enhanced and preserved to meet today’s technical standards and continue to deliver a high-quality, smooth visual experience for our players. PN: We didn’t need to overhaul the game’s content or visual assets. Instead, we leveraged the upgraded PSSR within our engine and rendering pipeline to enhance 4K image quality and deliver our Quality mode at 60FPS on PS5 Pro. The interesting challenge was finding the right balance between image quality, performance, and integration within an existing game that was originally built years before the PS5 Pro existed. The upgraded PSSR proved to be a very efficient solution, allowing us to maximize the new hardware’s capabilities while delivering a noticeable visual uplift and stronger performance without requiring extensive changes to the game’s content, making it an effective way to modernize the experience for PS5 Pro players. Play Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s The Most Requested update today on PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro!

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Assassin's Creed Valhalla gets New Game Plus and Stash inventory in "The Most Requested Update"
sources.text: A new Assassin's Creed Valhalla patch fittingly named "The Most Requested Update" just dropped, adding a range of features and systems that players have been asking for, including the fabled New Game Plus mode. Ubisoft shared the news on the PlayStation Blog , which notes that the PS5 Pro version of Assassin's Creed Valhalla now sports PSSR optimizations "to enhance 4K image quality and deliver our Quality mode at 60FPS on PS5 Pro." More detailed patch notes are available on Steam . New Game Plus is, as is often the case among modern Assassin's Creed fans, a headliner. "We know this has been a request for ages, and we appreciate your patience," writes Ubisoft, some four years after Valhalla's release. "You can now start your Viking quest all over again after completing the main story of Assassin’s Creed Valhalla. "To access NG+ you'll have to complete the Holy Day Quest, which is the last quest of the Hamtunscire region. (This is before the true ending of the game but since it is a very big game, we’ve decided to allow you to start NG+ a little bit earlier) Each iteration of NG+ will get progressively harder, offering new challenges to players who want to revisit the Viking Age again and again." Note that you will have to save the game post-update to unlock the NG+ option. With NG+ in mind, the cap on gear upgrades has been increased from 13 to 27, and upgrading is now tied to the new mithril resource. "You will need a lot of it," Ubisoft says. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more There's more progression to be had, too. "Extended Progression Mode" adds "a more granular sense of progression," by which Ubisoft means gear upgrades and Runes "increase Power by 1 point" while Masteries "increase Power every 5 skill points." "This mode is intended to increase the impact of your gear. The challenge is greater, but the reward is great for the mighty," the studio explains. Runes can also, themselves, be upgraded after today's update, and may reach the new "superior" tier. This, too, requires mithril. "The second addition to the rune forge is in the engrave page; we’ve added more than 300 available engravable runes, allowing players to engrave all of the perks that have been added since the release of Assassin’s Creed Valhalla, including DLCs and those purchased in the Helix Store," the patch notes add. For all that gear you're hoarding, Valhalla has also added a Stash inventory. "As we all know, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a big game, and it keeps getting bigger each year," Ubisoft reflects. So, the kind folks of Ravensthorpe have installed "a newly installed Stash which, when interacted with, will allow players to store any piece of gear and any rune from their inventory." The long-awaited update is rounded out by two new achievements for completionists (fully upgrade divine gear, and complete NG+), PSSR 2 support for PS5 Pro, and a long list of balance changes "trying to make dual wielding feel better, improve stat runes as well as balancing skill masteries and their bonuses." Ubisoft says it's done with Assassin's Creed remakes for now after Black Flag Resynced, and Assassin's Creed Hexe is "making steady progress" toward 2027 update Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: Nintendo says it isn't planning any more Switch 2 price hikes
sources.text: Nintendo, which unveiled the results of the first half of its fiscal year 2027 earlier today , has now said it has access to enough quantities of memory to manufacture more Switch 2 consoles. As a result, the platform holder does not plan to increase the price of the Switch 2. That's according to Reuters , citing Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa. Nintendo, which has so far sold 26m Switch 2 consoles, has already raised the price of the console earlier this year. The price hikes, which took effect on 1st September in the US, Canada, Japan and Europe, saw the console's price increase by $50 / €30 / ¥10,000. Although that was technically the first price hike for the console itself, prior to the Switch 2's launch last year, Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 accessories in the US as a result of the Trump Administration's tariffs. The reason that would cause Nintendo to raise prices again is the same that already caused rival PlayStation and Xbox to do so: AI-driven, global memory and storage shortages . PlayStation already raised PS5 and PS5 Pro prices , on several occasions . Xbox has likewise gone through multiple rounds of price hikes for its Series X and Series S consoles , with the most recent having taken place in August . That same crisis pushed one of Nintendo's longtime ROM suppliers to exit the business , opting instead to focus on the more lucrative business segments. ROM memory is used in Switch cartridges, though Nintendo hasn't commented on the news. Incidentally, Switch 2 hardware sales have been in decline for several quarters now compared to its banner launch in 2025. Still, Switch 2 sales are tracking ahead of the Switch 1.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: GOG Announces Road Rash Touch Up and a Publishing Arm for 'New Games With a Classic Soul'
sources.text: GOG is old enough to drink in the UK. To celebrate that milestone, the DRM-free storefront — which lets players do what they want to games once they own them, including sending them to other PCs, backing them up to hard drives, and even burning them onto discs to add to a physical collection — has announced a range of surprises. The company is currently on a mission to keep games available to play even after the seasons end and servers close down. Its GOG Patrons initiative has saved 300 old games, funding them to be made compatible with modern operating systems. Over 10,000 patrons have signed up to help. The latest game to benefit from this was Nox, the action RPG developed and published by Westwood Studios and EA back in 2000. “We dig deep into the code, fixing long-lasting bugs, adjusting screen resolutions, adding controller support, missing cutscenes and much, much more,” said Marcin Paczynski, senior business development manager. GOG has made over 1,700 fixes to old games in its preservation program. Next up, there’s good news for classic space sim and Mark Hamill fans. The Wing Commander series — Wing Commander 1-4 games, Prophecy Gold, and Privateer 2 — is getting an anniversary edition update. GOG collaborated with modders for Prophecy, with a goal of making the game more approachable, adding controller support to offer a new way to play. Each of these games comes with the legacy version and the touched up Anniversary Edition. For people who already own the original games on GOG, the Anniversary Editions are free to download at launch. Ahead of those updated space sims, there’s something new on GOG right now: Road Rash. The violent motorbike racing classic got the same treatment as Wing Commander, making it compatible with modern systems and control inputs. GOG also announced Retro Vibe, a publishing arm focused on “new games with a classic soul.” Retro Vibe releases include a VHS-fuzzed FPS with Max Payne-esque bullet time called Cop Bastard, a side-scrolling shooter with tough boss battles called The Looter, tactical cyberpunk RPG Shardpunk 2, boomer shooter with massive boomsticks Project Warlock: Lost Chapters, and the mysterious greyscale indie game After Hell Freezes Over. You can Wishlist the full lineup of games and check them out in more detail on GOG.com . It’s a site GOG is hoping you’ll spend more time on anyway, as the service is also introducing GOG Social, a new gaming forum integrated with your game library, allowing you to tag games in posts, taking readers directly to the store page. The forum has marked spoilers, threaded replies, reactions, post edits, media support, bookmarks, topic subscriptions, and more. Lastly, GOG Galaxy — GOG’s launcher that lets you combine your entire library from different stores into one space — is also coming to Linux. It’s landing with new customization and personalization options. Watch the entire showcase on the GOG YouTube channel . Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

Thanks to the discovery of a ‘physical media vault,’ EA was able to restore Road Rash and six Wing Commander titles for new Anniversary editions. Electronic Arts is launching 25 classic games on Steam, including “Anniversary Editions” of the motorcycle racer Road Rash and six Wing Commander titles. These Anniversary Editions preserve “the original look, feel and creative intent of the game” but also have quality-of-life updates to support modern systems and controls and improve performance, according to EA . The seven new editions were “inspired” by the discovery of a “physical media vault” with “thousands” of Betacam, VHS, and D1 tapes and “other media assets,” EA says. As part of the digitization process, EA was able to recover master FMV sequences and reedited them to restore more than 1,500 scenes from the games. The updated Wing Commander games also officially incorporate some community-made mods. You’ll be able to get the Road Rash and Wing Commander Anniversary editions for $9.99, and the other classic games, including Ultima and Crusader titles, will be available for $4.99. You can grab them on Steam, GOG, and the EA App.

sources.title: Nintendo Could Have A New Cartridge Problem On Its Hands

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: One of Nintendo's Switch and Switch 2 cartridge manufacturers is exiting the business, which could make physical games more expensive
sources.text: Macronix, longtime Nintendo hardware partner and one of the main producers of ROM memory, has announced it's leaving the business. ROM chips are key components in Switch and Switch 2 cartridges. Industry analyst David Gibson shared the news on X , which Macronix announced in its latest earnings call. The company plans to phase out ROM products entirely by the end of the third quarter of fiscal year 2026. As it stands, ROM products represent just 5 percent of Macronix's business, going off its reported sales for the third quarter. This is down significantly from 26 percent just one year ago. As a result, Macronix is shifting manufacturing capacity to instead focus on NOR (flash) and eMMC memory chips. It's worth noting that Macronix is not the only company Nintendo relies on for ROM memory. Nintendo also sources parts from Rohm Co. (Oki Semiconductor), but losing a key partner puts more pressure on the already strained supply, which could result in higher prices. As Gibson pointed out, that could also push more publishers - including Nintendo - to ship their games as Game-Key Cards instead, which do not include physical cartridges, avoiding the extra cost. Although not directly stated, this is likely another side effect of the ongoing, global AI-driven memory and storage crisis. On top of making many consumer products unaffordable for millions, causing the prices of game consoles to rise and putting GPUs out of reach for PC builders , the shortages have also caused major memory manufacturers to redirect their resources to business segments where demand is higher. Nearly one year ago, Micron, one of the three largest memory manufacturers in the world, announced it's exiting the consumer memory business and shutting down its Crucial brand . This could put more pressure on Nintendo, already one of the last holdouts continuing to invest in physical media, to raise prices of games even further or abandon cartridges. Just last month, Nintendo said it has no plans to ditch physical games , in the wake of rival Sony's decision to end disc manufacturing in 2028 .

stories.summary: Odencat will release a PlayStation 5 version of RPG adventure game Meg’s Monster on March …

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Meg’s Monster coming to PS5 on March 1, 2027
sources.text: Odencat will release a PlayStation 5 version of RPG adventure game Meg’s Monster on March 1, 2027, the companies announced. Meg’s Monster first launched for Xbox One, Switch, and PC via Steam on March 2, 2023, followed by iOS and Android on May 7, 2026. Additionally, the Meg’s Monster Complete Edition bundle containing the base game and downloadable content “Lost Memories” will be available for Switch on November 19. Both the downloadable content and bundle will be available for the PlayStation 5 version when it releases in 2027. Here is an overview of the game, via Odencat: Welcome to the Underworld—a land of monsters and mutants who eat humans for breakfast. One such monster—a hulking ogre by the name of Roy—has no interest in eating humans. But one day, he and his best friend Golan stumble upon a lost little girl named Meg, and discover something truly terrifying: the moment she starts wailing in fear, a blood-red hue washes over the sky, and the earth itself begins to tremble and quake. That’s right: this small girl’s tears hold the power to bring forth the apocalypse—and the only way to stop it is for them to help find her mother so she can make it safely back home. Meg’s Monster is a short, story-driven JRPG with a big twist. Players control Roy, who begins the game with 99,999 HP and is virtually untouchable—but the real concern is keeping Meg safe, because if she starts crying, it’s game over for everyone. Players will have to master the unique mechanics and mini-games baked into each battle, all while protecting Meg and using her favorite toys to keep her pacified. Over the course of their journey together, Roy and Meg will encounter a host of quirky and colorful characters, all lovingly rendered in Odencat’s trademark vibrant pixel aesthetic that makes even scary monsters look cute. There’s plenty of drama and intrigue to be found here—and even previously defeated enemies can be befriended through optional sub-events. What begins as a relatively simple and heartwarming story about two unlikely friends ultimately expands into something much greater, as Roy and Meg slowly begin to unravel the mysteries surrounding the Underworld and themselves. The result is an emotional journey that, like any good storybook, will remain in your heart for years to come.

sources.title: WoW: Forever's massive pre-launch balance patch breaks from the chains Classic power, increasing 'the health of higher level creatures to compensate'
sources.text: "Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options." "Over the course of Beta, we came to the realization that trying to hold ourselves roughly to Classic power budgets for each class meant that every new element we added needed to come at the expense of something else. Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options." "So over the last two weeks, we’ve raised damage on classes across the game, and have increased the health of higher level creatures to compensate. This additional 'headroom' has allowed us to tune things to a place that we hope feels better overall," via the official WoW forums. This honestly makes the most sense to me—yes, there are some elements of Classic I want WoW: Forever to preserve. The slower, more relaxed pace and the time-to-kill (something that has been maintained to a deliberate, intentional degree ) of oldschool MMOs, for one. But if you're gonna do Classic+, you shouldn't have to limit yourself to the power and ability budgets that came out 20 years ago. You might as well go whole-hog and try to get things feeling a little more interesting, if still along the lines of that vanilla feeling. The statement linked above, which was posted in a series of pre-release patch notes, continues: "Beyond that, some of this round of changes reflects areas where we were likely hasty in turning to Burning Crusade or Wrath-era solutions rather than carving out new ones that better fit into the Forever combat model. "Our aim in class design is not perfect numerical equality, but rather for every class to feel valuable to the groups they join, with powerful, unforgettable moments brought on by mastering them. In Forever this is accomplished by doubling down on the strengths and differences that make each class unique, rather than overly unifying them." Hear hear! Homogenisation is the death of interesting class design, and I've certainly played MMOs where that's been a massive problem (I am very much hoping that FF14's Evolved job reworks hit this mark). The patch notes themselves are interesting, too. For starters, tanks have had their threat bonuses absolutely ramped. Warriors' defensive stance has spiked from a 30% to an 80% increase and Druid's bear form has been bumped from 50% to 115%, with similar threat generation buffs for Paladins. This is primarily to offset the removal of Blessing of Salvation, which seems smart to me—you probably shouldn't be balancing threat generation writ large over the spell of one class. Rogues now have an ability called "Shank", an off-hand weapon energy generation tool—which has a different flavour for each specialisation. Combat rogues get more energy from it, Subtlety rogues can get extra combo points, and Assassination rogues can use it to debuff enemies to make them more vulnerable to their poisons. This is just skimming the top of the iceberg—there have been a ton of changes: "We’ve used the data and feedback gathered during Beta testing to get everything tuned to a reasonable place. However, the only true test of that tuning is the game itself. With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don’t plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data. And this is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue to evolve over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004."
